typical_lesion_features: Blackheads or whiteheads; red papules; pustules; sometimes deeper nodules
duration: Often recurrent or persistent over weeks to years
pain: Variable; more likely with deep or inflamed lesions
newExposure: Variable; some products or medicines may worsen acne-like eruptions
distinctive_clue: Comedones (blackheads or whiteheads) may be a clue, not proof
safety_note: Seek medical assessment for severe pain, rapid worsening, or fever
interpretation_limit: Symptoms overlap with other conditions; not a diagnosis

typical_lesion_features: Superficial sores or blisters that may rupture and form yellowish or honey-coloured crusts
duration: Often develops over days; progression varies
location: Often around nose and mouth; may occur elsewhere
bleeding: Variable; sores may become raw or bleed
discharge: May be present; sores can ooze or crust
blisters: May be present, depending on type
fever: Usually absent in limited cases; possible in more extensive illness
sensitiveArea: Variable; lesions near eyes or mucosal areas need prompt assessment
newExposure: Variable; close contact may be relevant
distinctive_clue: Honey-coloured crusting may be a clue, but is not specific
safety_note: Seek prompt assessment for spreading lesions, fever, worsening pain, or lesions near eyes
interpretation_limit: A clinician may need to distinguish it from other conditions

typical_lesion_features: Small, smooth, firm, dome-shaped bumps, often with a central dimple
duration: May persist for months; course varies
location: Can occur on many body areas
pain: Usually absent unless inflamed or irritated
sensitiveArea: Variable; genital-area lesions should be assessed
newExposure: Close skin contact or shared items may be relevant
distinctive_clue: Small pearly or skin-coloured bumps with a central dimple may be a clue
safety_note: Seek advice for genital lesions, extensive disease, or immune-system concerns
interpretation_limit: Other bumps can look similar; appearance alone is insufficient

typical_lesion_features: Well-defined raised patches with scale; colour varies with skin tone
duration: Often chronic, with flares and improvement
location: Commonly elbows, knees, scalp, lower back; other sites possible
spreading: Variable; patches may enlarge or new patches develop
pain: Variable; cracks or inflamed areas may hurt
bleeding: Possible if skin cracks or is scratched
discharge: Not typical for ordinary plaque psoriasis
fever: Not typical; fever with rash needs assessment
sensitiveArea: Variable; folds or genital skin can be affected
newExposure: Not defining; triggers or medicines may affect flares
distinctive_clue: Persistent, sharply bordered scaly plaques may be a clue
safety_note: Widespread redness, pus, fever, severe pain, or rapid deterioration needs prompt assessment
interpretation_limit: Can resemble other inflammatory or infectious conditions

typical_lesion_features: Raised, itchy wheals or welts that often change shape or location; individual wheals usually fade within 24 hours
duration: Individual wheals are usually temporary; episodes may recur
spreading: Wheals may appear in new areas; not the same as an expanding fixed lesion
swelling: Swelling may occur; deeper swelling is possible
fever: Not typical; fever or feeling very unwell needs assessment
sensitiveArea: Swelling of lips, tongue, mouth, or throat is urgent
newExposure: May follow foods, medicines, infections, stings, or other triggers; a trigger may not be found
distinctive_clue: Very itchy raised wheals that fade or move over hours may be a clue
safety_note: Breathing difficulty or tongue/throat swelling is an emergency
interpretation_limit: A single photo may not capture rapidly changing hives

typical_lesion_features: Well-defined lighter or depigmented patches; hair in patches may also lose colour
duration: Often persistent; patches may remain stable or change
location: Can affect many areas, often face, hands, and body openings
spreading: Variable; new patches or enlargement may occur
sensitiveArea: Patches may occur near eyes, mouth, or genital areas; location alone does not indicate emergency
previousOccurrence: May be present; personal or family history may be relevant
distinctive_clue: Loss of pigment without typical scale or discharge may be a clue
safety_note: New or changing pigment loss should be assessed if diagnosis is uncertain
interpretation_limit: Other pigment disorders and post-inflammatory colour changes can resemble vitiligo

typical_lesion_features: Rough or firm raised papules; some may have tiny dark dots; appearance varies by site
duration: May persist for months or longer
location: Hands, fingers, feet, and other sites
pain: Variable; plantar warts may hurt with pressure
sensitiveArea: Genital or mucosal lesions need professional assessment
newExposure: Skin contact or shared surfaces may be relevant
distinctive_clue: Rough, firm surface may be a clue; tiny dark dots sometimes occur
safety_note: Seek assessment for bleeding, rapid changes, severe pain, facial/genital lesions, or uncertainty
interpretation_limit: Some growths can resemble warts; appearance alone is insufficient
